claims.claim: Eustathius of Antioch was the bishop (later patriarch) of Antioch, serving roughly 324–330, and was a native of Side in Pamphylia, dying about 337.
He was a leading opponent of Arianism at the Council of Nicaea and was later deposed and exiled for alleged Sabellianism.
The homily is addressed to the Christian faithful, opening with “Ἀκούσωμεν ἀγαπητοί” (“Let us listen, beloved ones”), indicating a congregational audience.
The homily is also included in the Patrologia Graeca (vol. XVIII, cols. 675‑698), providing wider scholarly access.
